pool.text: The Melanesian Brotherhood, which has offices in Honiara, was established by Ini Kopuria.
American forces defeated the Japanese in a major battle at Henderson Field.
American artillery and small arms destroyed a Japanese ship in shallow waters.
Honiara became the administrative centre and capital of the British Solomon Islands Protectorate.
Holy Cross Cathedral, a large Roman Catholic church, was consecrated in Honiara.
The Cathedral Church of St Barnabas was consecrated in Honiara.
Honiara became the new capital of the independent Solomon Islands.
Honiara remained a small town in population terms for a capital city.
A capital territory comprising the metropolitan area of Honiara was proclaimed.
The Solomon Islands Parliament Building, built with American aid, was inaugurated.
The country earned a specific amount of money from tourism.
The Melanesia Arts and Crafts Festival was held for the first time in Honiara.
Tourism in the city and nation accounted for a small percentage of total GDP.
A coup attempt resulted in violent fighting between ethnic Malaitans and Guadalcanal natives.
Violence ensued in the city streets when two New Zealand diplomats and others were murdered.
The Regional Assistance Mission to Solomon Islands was invited into the country.
Riots broke out following the election of Snyder Rini as Prime Minister.
The hospital accident and emergency department served a large number of patients.
David Vunagi formally took over the post of archbishop at the Cathedral Church of St Barnabas.
A bookstore called Save Senta opened at Point Cruz in Honiara.
